tldr: Use Excel for Mac to organize your 80 to 150 open claims files.
Apply keyboard shortcuts to save time on formatting and data entry.

blocks.text: Setting up your claims tracker in Excel

Your spreadsheet is your command center. Start by creating a clear header row. Include columns for Claim Number, Insured Name, Date of Loss, and Status. Use the View menu to select Freeze Panes so your headers stay visible as you scroll. If you deal with many files, use Format as Table to enable quick filtering.

blocks.text: Speeding up data entry on Mac

Keyboard shortcuts make a difference. Use ⌘ + T to quickly turn a range into a table. Use ⌥ + ⌘ + V to open the Paste Special menu. If you need to fill a formula down a long column, select the range and press ⌘ + D. These small habits save minutes every hour.
Using voice to manage your day

You are often away from your keyboard or busy with phone calls. Hold the fn key to dictate notes directly into a cell. If you are unsure where a feature lives, hold ⌥ + ⌘ and ask Lazur. It will circle the button on your screen. This keeps your eyes on the data instead of the menus.

Organize your data with conditional formatting. Highlight rows based on status, like overdue or pending. Use Data Validation to create drop down lists for status updates. This prevents typos and keeps your reports consistent. You can also use the Group and Outline features to hide completed claims without deleting them.

Documentation is the most important part of your role. Create a column for notes or timestamps. Use the shortcut ⌃ + ; to insert the current date. This provides a clear record of when you checked a file or sent an email. Keep your spreadsheet updated daily to satisfy regulatory requirements.

faq.question: Can I use Excel on my Mac for all my claims?
faq.answer: Yes, Excel for Mac is fully capable of handling large datasets and complex formulas. Ensure you are on a recent version of macOS to keep the app running smoothly.

faq.question: How do I stop Excel from changing my claim numbers?
faq.answer: Select the cells, go to the Home tab, and change the number format to Text. This prevents Excel from removing leading zeros.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Excel?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your Mac screen. You can ask it to point at menu items or guide you through tasks in Excel, but it does not edit your spreadsheet files directly.
